newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods turn narrowly mixed on impasse.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods turn narrowly mixed on impasse.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices turned narrowly mixed with a stand-off between buyers and sellers keeping activity light early Wednesday.

Sellers refused to cut offers, despite a slide in all three legs of the energy complex Wednesday. But buyers, noting that crude was down 62 cents at 1100 PDT/1800 GMT, maintained their bearish positions.
"Sellers have not been happy with prices...and buyers are trying to push (them) lower," one Northwest-based trader said.
NYMEX gasoline for November delivery fell about 1.88 cents to 65.20 cents a gallon.
Heating oil joined the downward trend by shedding around 2.22 cents a gallon to 70.85.
Low sulphur diesel in Los Angeles trimmed a half cent to 71/71.50 cents a gallon. Jet fuel bids climbed 0.50 cent to 67.50 cents a gallon, with offers flat at 68 cents.
CARB diesel in L.A. was notionally unchanged at 83/84 cents, with November parcels heard bid at 79 cents.
Los Angeles CARB regular gasoline eased a cent to 67/68 cents a gallon, after a flat afternoon Tuesday.
Conventional regular gasoline in L.A. stayed 62/63 cents.
